t: People Management v28 - Configuring HR Admin Field Options - User Guide
f: People Management v28 - Configuring HR Admin Field Options - User Guide.pdf
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide detailed guidance on the HR Admin Field Options functionality that is available in People Management. What are HR Admin Field Options? Display Options This feature provides the ability to control the display and use of several key fields on employee and contract records on CoreHR.
ss: HR Admin Field Options in People Management lets you control which fields display and whether they're mandatory on key HR screens like the New Hire wizard, Replace Contract wizard, Key Information, and Contracts pages. You can hide optional fields, make fields mandatory (marked with a red asterisk), or leave them optional, and these changes apply immediately across all users in the system. Additionally, this feature allows you to customize how dropdown lists appear—showing either just the description or both the code and description from reference data. Open this guide when you need to configure field visibility and requirements for employee and contract records in CoreHR.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring HR Admin Field Options in People Management v28, a feature that allows administrators to control the display and requirements of key fields across multiple HR screens. The document covers two main configuration types: Display Options, which control field visibility and mandatory status on screens such as the Create Person Wizard, Key Information, and Continuous Service screens, and Combo Field Options, which determine whether dropdown lists display descriptions only or code-description combinations. To access these configurations, users navigate to the Data Centre widget, open HR Admin Setup Settings, and select HR Admin Field Options. The guide explains how to update Display Options by selecting the appropriate screen, searching for required fields, and using the Edit button to toggle the Hide and Mandatory settings, with changes applying globally to all system users immediately upon saving. For each field, administrators can set either Hide or Mandatory status but not both simultaneously, though certain system-required fields have protected Mandatory settings that cannot be modified. The Display Options functionality specifically applies to fields on HR Admin screens including the New Hire wizard, Replace Contract wizard, Additional Contract wizard, Rehire wizard, End Person/End Contract, and Contracts screens, and does not affect similar fields appearing elsewhere in CoreHR such as the Employee Profile or dashboard. This guide is designed for HR administrators responsible for tailoring the system configuration to their organization's specific field requirements and data entry workflows.

ss: HR Process Task Lists in CoreHR define mandatory and optional steps that must be completed during New Starter, New Contract, Additional Contract, Rehire, or Leaver processes. Open this guide when you need to set up or configure task lists, assign step owners, manage user access permissions, or understand how to complete task lists within People Management. Different task lists can be created for each process type to ensure all necessary employee and contract information is captured in a structured workflow.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive guidance on configuring and using HR Process Task Lists in CoreHR People Management v28, covering setup procedures, available steps, access management, and task completion workflows. Task lists are automated workflows triggered when new contracts are assigned to employees through New Starter, New Contract, Additional Contract, Rehire, or Leaver processes in People Management, presenting users with mandatory and optional steps that must be completed before finalizing the employment process. Additional sections cover access control for contract task lists, including menu options to view, update, and complete task lists, along with managing access for leavers and general user permissions. Open this document when you need to grant or modify user permissions for HR data (employees and contracts), pay data (salaries and allowances), or understand how data access restrictions work in your People Management system.
sl: This user guide for People Management v28 explains how to configure and manage user access to employee, contract, and salary data within the CoreHR system. The document covers two distinct access categories: Menu Profiles, which control access to system functionality such as dashboards, screens, buttons, and widgets aligned to user roles like HR administrators or payroll administrators, and Data Access, which controls access to actual records including Employees, Posts, and Salaries. User access to employee, post, and contract data is managed through the Organisational Structure, allowing administrators to grant access at specific levels such as Company, Division, Management Unit, or Department, enabling granular control over which records different users can view. The guide provides detailed instructions for granting HR access (covering Employees, Contracts, and Posts) and Pay access (covering Salaries & Allowances), as well as assigning default menu profiles to users. Additional configuration options are described for controlling employee visibility based on current substantive contracts and displaying future transfers to users with appropriate access permissions. The document includes an appendix detailing what data security access controls across various screens and functions, including the Command Centre widget, Employee Screen, Employee Record Contract List, Contracts Screen, Advanced Employee Setup, and salary and deduction records. This guide is intended for system administrators and HR configuration personnel responsible for setting up user permissions and data access controls in People Management.

t: People Management v28 - Contract Amendments - User Guide
f: People Management v28 - Contract Amendments - User Guide.pdf
s: The purpose of this guide is to provide instructions on how to amend an employee’s existing contract on People Management. This guide does not provide instruction on: • how to replace a contract. • how to award an additional contract. • how to create a salary amendment independent of a contract amendment. Please refer to the relevant user guides for the above tasks if required.
ss: Contract amendments in People Management allow you to modify an employee's existing contract terms, including organizational structure (cost centre, location, workgroup), job details (title, category, post type), and contracted hours or weeks that affect salary. Use this guide when you need to record date-driven changes to employee contracts—whether they impact salary (such as hour reductions requiring pro-rated adjustments) or have no salary impact (such as work group or location changes). The guide walks through the two-step amendment wizard and explains which fields to update based on whether the change affects the employee's salary, plus how to track contract history and timelines.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for amending employee contracts within the People Management v28 system, covering both salary-impacting and non-salary-impacting changes that HR administrators need to make to existing employee records. The document explains when contract amendments are necessary and walks users through the standard process: accessing the Command Centre widget, searching for the employee, navigating to the Contracts tab, and clicking Update in the Amendments section, which launches a 2-step Edit Contract wizard. For amendments with no salary impact (such as changes to work group, cost centre, location, or job category), users can modify organizational structure and contract fields while avoiding fields like Contracted Hours, Contracted Weeks, FTE, and Standard Hours that would trigger salary recalculations. For amendments with salary impact (such as reduced hours requiring pro-rated salary adjustments), the process is similar but users must update the salary-related fields and ensure the Effective Date and mandatory Reason fields are properly completed to track when and why the amendment occurred. The guide also addresses related tasks including deleting contracts, managing replacement and additional contracts, deleting amendments, and switching posts, while tracking all changes through the Contract Timeline/History feature so administrators can review the complete amendment sequence for any employee. This document is intended for HR administrators and payroll professionals who regularly manage employee contract changes within the People Management system.

t: People Management v28 - Contract Start Date Corrections - User Guide v1.0

s: Purpose of the Guide This document provides guidance on how to change an employee’s start date on CoreHR, including: • How to change their start date. • How to update their contract start date. • What elements of the employee’s record get updated. • What elements of the employee’s record do not get automatically updated. Overview of Start Date Corrections 1.2.1. What Contracts can be Updated?
ss: Contract Start Date Corrections in People Management allows you to update an employee's start date in CoreHR for new hires, rehires, and additional contracts, with the system automatically adjusting related contract elements like salary, allowances, pension, BIK, deductions, and organizational roles. Open this guide when you need to correct an employee's contract start date and understand which employee records will be updated, which cannot be changed (such as replacement contracts or those already processed on payroll), and how the changes will impact payroll processing. The guide walks through the step-by-step process of amending a contract start date and details what happens to each associated contract element during the correction.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for correcting employee contract start dates within the CoreHR People Management v28 system, covering the complete process from initiating changes through understanding system impacts. The document explains how to change a start date by opening an employee record, navigating to the Contracts section, and selecting the "Amend Contract Start Date" button, which launches a prompt where users enter the new date and proceed to a detailed review screen. The guide specifies which contracts can be modified—including new hires, rehires, and additional contracts—and clearly identifies restrictions, such as replacement contracts and contracts already processed on payroll that cannot be updated through this functionality. When a start date is changed, the system automatically reviews and updates multiple associated contract elements including salary, allowances, cost allocations, pension information, benefits in kind (BIK), deductions, substantive dates, and organizational roles, with each element flagged to indicate whether it requires manual review, automatic updating, deletion, end-date input, or no action. The guide addresses payroll integration by explaining that while changes to pay-related elements flow through to payroll records and the start date and latest start date fields update automatically, restrictions are in place to prevent negative payroll impacts when payroll is currently in process or has already been processed. HR professionals and payroll administrators responsible for onboarding corrections and contract management would typically use this document to ensure accurate start date changes and understand the cascading effects on employee records and payroll systems.

ss: The Employee Files feature in People Management allows HR administrators to upload, organize, and manage employee documents and contract-related files within an employee's HR record. This guide covers how to access the Files screen, add and delete documents, manage different document types (categorized as either Person or Contract level), and configure viewing permissions for administrators, employees, and managers. Use this guide when you need to upload employee documentation, understand file access security options, or manage which files different user roles can view or upload. The guide also explains how files can be uploaded directly by administrators, automatically generated by the system, or uploaded by employees and managers through their respective profile screens.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instruction on managing employee files within CoreHR's People Management system version 28, covering all aspects of document storage and access for HR administrators. The document explains how files are uploaded through multiple channels—directly by HR administrators via the People Management > Files screen, automatically through the Document and Email Generation feature, or by employees and managers through their respective My Profile and Employee Profile screens. The guide details the Files screen navigation, which is accessed from the Command Centre > Employees screen by selecting an employee's record and then clicking the Files option in the left menu, where users can view file details including File Name, Document Type, upload date, and file size. It describes key file management tasks including how to add individual employee files and contract-specific files, delete files, and handle multiple file uploads simultaneously, along with viewing files generated automatically by CoreHR. The document outlines security configuration options for administrator access to files, including either unrestricted access to all Document Types or restricted access based on specific Document Type permissions. Document Types themselves are categorized as either Person (files linked directly to an employee) or Contract (files linked to specific employee contracts), with configurable settings determining whether employees and managers can view and upload documents against each type. The guide is designed primarily for HR administrators, managers with devolved People Management tasks, and system administrators responsible for configuring document access permissions across different user roles.

In CoreHR, the hr administrator’s access to employees on the system is restricted based on their designated HR Access. This HR Access...
ss: Employee transfers in People Management allow HR administrators to request moving an employee from one contract to another when they lack direct access to the employee's current record. This process is essential when an HR administrator needs to transfer an employee into a department or organizational unit they manage, but the employee's current contract exists in a department they cannot access. Use this guide to learn how to create transfer requests, search for employees and positions, submit requests for approval, and complete the transfer once authorized. The guide also covers how to view, approve, reject, or cancel transfer requests depending on your role and access level.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing employee transfers within the People Management v28 system, specifically addressing situations where HR administrators need to transfer employees across organizational units to which they lack direct access. The document covers the complete transfer lifecycle, including how to create transfer requests by searching for employees and posts, viewing submitted requests with access to current and proposed contract details, canceling requests, and approving or rejecting transfers through the Transfers window accessible via the Command Centre widget. The guide explains the role of HR Access restrictions in CoreHR, which limit administrator visibility to employees based on designated organizational units such as Company, Department, and Division, and describes how transfer requests solve the problem of moving employees between departments when the initiating administrator lacks access to the employee's current contract. Key processes outlined include accessing transfer requests through three tabs (Incoming Transfers, Outgoing Transfers, and Request Transfer), searching for employees and posts to create new requests, viewing transfer history and proposed contracts, placing requests on hold, and completing the transfer to generate the required replacement contract. This guide is intended for HR administrators who need to move employees across departmental boundaries within their organization, particularly those without direct access to an employee's current contract but with access to the destination post.

s: The purpose of this guide is to provide detailed guidance on how to set up a new hire on People Management. There are a number of ways in which a new hire can be setup on People Management, depending on the posts that an organisation will use as the foundation for the employee’s contract. Therefore , this guide will provide steps on how to complete the setup for the following Post Profile / Post Appointment types: • Auto-Authorised Post Profile • Auto-Commenced Post...
ss: People Management v28 covers the complete new hire contract setup process in CoreHR, guiding you through creating employee records using different post profile types (Auto-Authorised, Auto-Commenced, and Planned & Authorised appointments). Use this guide when onboarding new employees to learn how to search for the correct post, verify the employee doesn't already exist in the system, and capture their personal information through the New Employee Wizard. You'll also find instructions for commencing appointments and copying new starter records to streamline the setup process.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for setting up new employees in People Management v28, covering the complete new hire contract process from initial search through employee creation. The document details three distinct setup workflows based on Post Profile types: Auto-Authorised Appointments, Auto-Commenced Appointments, and Planned & Authorised Post Appointments, each involving specific sequences of steps through screens such as the New Employee Wizard, Duplicate Employee Check, and Commence Appointment. Users begin by clicking the New Starter button on the Command Centre widget, then search for Post Profiles using either a quick search by Post Number or Post Title, or a more detailed Post Filter utilizing organizational hierarchy fields and structure selection. The process includes a mandatory duplicate employee check that searches by Forename, Surname, or PPS/NI Number to identify whether an employee already exists in the system as an active or dormant record. The New Employee Wizard contains a multi-step creation process beginning with Person Information, where users input mandatory fields including Title, Forename, Surname, Date of Birth, Gender, Nationality, Email Address, Phone, Mobile, and address details, with some fields like Initials, Age, and Retirement Date automatically calculated or populated. This guide is designed for HR personnel and administrators responsible for onboarding new employees within organizations using CoreHR's People Management system, and it excludes coverage of Post Profile creation itself, referring users to separate Managing Post Profiles documentation for that process.

t: People Management v28 - Payroll Instructional Forms - User Guide v1.0
f: People Management v28 - Payroll Instructional Forms - User Guide v1.0.pdf
s: Purpose of the Guide This guide is used to explain how to use the Payroll Instruction Forms via People Management. In order to capture and automatically share pay-affecting information with Payroll, as part of the joiner/mover/leaver processes e.g. holidays to be paid to a leaver, student loans for a new hire etc. Within this User Guide you will learn how to: • Create a custom form. • Add a new HR task list item of Payroll Instructional Form. • Assign a specific Org Role...
ss: Payroll Instructional Forms in People Management v28 are used to capture and share pay-affecting information with the Payroll team during joiner, mover, and leaver processes—such as holiday balances, student loans, tax code changes, bonuses, and pension updates. This guide walks you through creating custom forms, adding them to HR Task Lists, configuring access restrictions, and viewing completed forms on the Pay Portal and Payroll Dashboard. Open this document when you need to set up or complete payroll instruction workflows, or when you're processing employee changes that require payroll team notification.
sl: This user guide explains how to use and configure Payroll Instructional Forms within People Management v28 to capture pay-affecting employee information and automatically share it with the Payroll team during joiner, mover, and leaver processes. The document covers both end-user tasks and administrator configuration, enabling users to complete forms via the HR Task List by navigating to the Command Centre widget, selecting the Outstanding Processes view, and choosing the appropriate employee tab (such as Leavers) to access and complete the Payroll Instructional Form screen. Payroll Instructional Forms function as a communication method for HR to notify Payroll of details that affect employee payroll records, including holiday balance adjustments, student loan payments, PAYE or tax code changes, overtime hours, bonus payments, pension changes, pay awards, cost allocation changes, and processing of cancellations or manual payments. The guide provides step-by-step instructions for creating custom forms by adding sections and fields, integrating these forms into the HR Task List, restricting form access as needed, and assigning specific organizational roles as task owners through the configuration sections. Users can view the instructional form history on the Pay Portal and access related screens such as Leaver Details through the Actions button, while payroll teams access completed forms through the Pay Portal dashboard. This guide is designed for HR professionals and payroll administrators who need to manage employee information flows during employment lifecycle events and for system configurators who need to set up custom forms tailored to their organization's business lines or employee groupings.

t: People Management v28 - Pension by Appointment - User Guide v1.0
f: People Management v28 - Pension by Appointment - User Guide v1.0.pdf
s: Purpose of the Guide Note This guide is only applicable if an organisation is managing the assignment of pension schemes for employees at contract level, rather than person level. Please refer to the relevant Payroll training resources for guidance on managing pension scheme assignments at employee level. This document provides guidance on how to manage pension schemes for employees by directly assigning these to their contract records.
ss: Pension by Appointment in CoreHR allows you to assign pension schemes directly to employee contracts rather than at the person level, enabling different schemes for employees with multiple contracts. This guide covers how to link pension schemes to post profiles, assign them to individual employee contracts, amend existing assignments, and manage scheme endings or deletions. Use this guide if your organization configures CoreHR to manage pension assignments at the contract or appointment level rather than the employee level. Open this document when you need step-by-step instructions for setting up post profile pension schemes, assigning pensions to specific contracts, or making changes to existing pension scheme assignments in People Management.
sl: This user guide for People Management v28 provides comprehensive instructions for managing pension scheme assignments at the contract or appointment level rather than at the employee person level, which is an alternative configuration option in CoreHR. The document covers the complete workflow for pension management by appointment, including linking pension schemes to post profile records through the Post Profile Maintenance screen (option 11 – Post Pension Schemes), assigning pension schemes to individual employee contracts, amending existing assignments, and ending or deleting pension scheme assignments. A key distinction explained is that the "Pension by Appointment" approach allows different pension schemes to be assigned to different contracts for the same employee, and automatically ends pension assignments when a contract ends, whereas "Pension by Person" assigns schemes directly to employee records in Payroll and remains independent of contract changes. The guide specifically details step-by-step processes such as adding a post pension scheme by searching for "Post Pension Maintenance" in the Data Centre and completing fields including pension scheme code and start dates, as well as ending and deleting schemes from post profiles. Additional processes covered include assigning pension schemes to employee contracts through the Command Centre widget, amending existing assignments, and managing pension scheme assignment terminations through either contract end dates or direct ending. This document is intended for HR and People Management users who need to configure and maintain pension scheme assignments within organizations that have enabled the "Pension by Appointment" configuration in CoreHR, as distinct from organizations using the Payroll-managed "Pension by Person" approach.

This allows for the completion of contract details for successful applicants in a recruitment campaign for: • New hires • New contracts for existing employees o Replacement contracts o Additional contracts • Rehires In order for this option to be used, the successful applicant must be linked to a job offer in Recruitment and flagged as having accepted this...
ss: The Successful Applicants feature in People Management handles contract creation for candidates who have accepted job offers through the Recruitment module, covering new hires, replacement contracts, additional contracts for existing employees, and rehires. HR administrators use this tool to access a filtered list of applicants ready to process, view job offer details, link applicants to employee records, and manage contract setup before employees start. Open this guide when you need to onboard successful recruitment candidates into the People Management system or create new contract records for existing staff taking on additional or replacement roles. The document explains how to navigate the Successful Applicants screen, complete applicant linking, and process different types of new appointments.
sl: This user guide for People Management v28 provides comprehensive instructions on managing successful job applicants through the contract creation process, applicable only when the Recruitment module is in use. The document covers four main applicant categories: new hires, replacement contracts for existing employees, additional contracts for existing employees, and rehires. Users access the Successful Applicants feature by navigating to the Command Centre widget and clicking the View button for Applicants, which displays a filtered list based on the HR administrator's designated access permissions (such as departmental or budget restrictions). The Successful Applicants screen presents summary-level applicant details including Name, Applicant Number, Personnel Number (for existing employees), Vacancy ID, Vacancy Name, Start Date, and Post, with an Action column indicating whether the applicant is a New Starter or New Appointment. Each applicant record offers several options: View Contract (a read-only view of job offer details from the Recruitment module displayed across a 3-step Applicant Offer Screen), Applicant Link (which allows linking new starters to existing employee records or other applicant records via dropdown menus), and Decline Job Offer (which removes the applicant from processing while maintaining their recruitment record status). The guide explains that applicants only appear on this screen once a job offer has been made and accepted, and they are removed if the offer is subsequently declined. This document is designed for HR administrators who need to process successful applicants through People Management after recruitment activities have been completed, ensuring proper contract setup and employee record linkage.

This guide walks you through creating new structures from scratch, editing existing ones, and configuring auto-fill functionality that populates hierarchy information across staff requests, post profiles, and contracts. Open this document when you need to establish or modify how your organisation's reporting lines, departments, and cost centres are structured in the system. It's essential for HR administrators setting up CoreHR for the first time or making structural changes to accommodate organisational changes.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive guidance for CoreHR administrators on configuring and managing organisational structures within the People Management v28 system. The document covers the complete lifecycle of organisational structure management, including creating new structures, editing existing ones, defining and configuring reference data items, and establishing linked organisational hierarchies. Key configuration tasks detailed include adding and removing levels within structures, setting hierarchy indicators, defining initial values, configuring hide indicators, and selecting display modes before activating the structure. The guide addresses the standard reference data elements used in organisational structures—specifically Company, Division, Management Unit, Department, Work Group, Cost Centre, Location, and User Fields 1-5—as well as the process for linking these elements through hierarchy maintenance. Additional configuration options covered include default collapse/expand settings for hierarchy display and the Auto-Fill Hierarchy functionality, which automatically populates hierarchy information across the Staff Request Wizard, Post Profile Wizard, and Contract Wizards. This guide is intended for HR administrators and system configurators who need to establish and maintain organisational structures to support People Management operations in CoreHR environments.

The guide covers the entire migration workflow including file processing, error resolution, data clearing, and security controls. Reference this document if you're managing large-scale data imports or need to understand the new v28 features like background file processing and enhanced data validation.
sl: This user guide for the People XD Data Migration Tool v28 provides comprehensive instructions on bulk importing organizational data during system implementation or upgrades, covering employees, contracts, occupational absences, and payroll cumulative history through a set of 26 available templates. The document explains the purpose and functionality of the Data Migration Tool, distinguishes between data migration and updates, and details the v28 enhancements including new background processing of files, enhanced data migration file templates, a Data Migration Options Widget, improved file download capabilities, and new file statuses for People Management with post-validation features. Users will learn how to locate the Data Migration Tool within the system, download templates and helper files, complete templates using pipe "|" delimiters for CSV files, upload files, monitor uploading status, process records, and handle upload errors through the Load the Template File, Processing the Records, and Fixing Upload Errors sections. Open this guide when you need to review an employee's absence history, calculate absence-related pay adjustments, or understand how absence rules and entitlements are applied across different absence types. The guide includes UK-specific configuration requirements and provides detailed explanations of search functions, display options, and calculation methodologies for absence pay processing.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive documentation for the PeopleXD Payroll Absence Pay Enhancement feature, designed to help payroll professionals manage and track employee absence information and related pay calculations. The document covers multiple key screens and processes, including the Absence Summary Screen, the Absence Pay Per Period Screen (which allows searching and filtered viewing of absence pay data across different periods), the WFM Absences Current Period Screen for tracking current workforce management absences, and the Information Per Absence Type Screen with entitlement windows and recent/future absence tracking. t: PeopleXD Payroll- Configure Auto Enrolment V1.0
f: PeopleXD Payroll- Configure Auto Enrolment V1.0.pdf
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure auto enrolment. This will include how to set parameters used to control auto enrolment. Auto Enrolment is a government initiative and requires every employer of staff normally working in the UK to put their qualifying staff into a workplace pension scheme and to make contributions towards their employee's pension.
ss: Auto Enrolment is a UK government requirement to automatically enroll eligible employees into a workplace pension scheme, and this guide walks you through configuring it in PeopleXD Payroll. The document covers setting up auto enrolment parameters—including staging periods, age thresholds, earnings eligibility, and default pension schemes—as well as configuring pay codes, pay groups, pension schemes, and pension rules to control how employees are enrolled. Open this if you need to set up or adjust auto enrolment settings for your organization, define which pay codes and earnings count toward eligibility, or configure pension scheme options and re-enrollment rules. This is essential reading for payroll administrators implementing auto enrolment compliance in PeopleXD.
sl: This document serves as a comprehensive configuration guide for setting up auto enrolment functionality within the PeopleXD Payroll system, specifically addressing the UK government's mandatory workplace pension scheme requirement. The guide covers eight distinct configuration tasks accessed through the Settings > UK Tax Rates > General > Auto Enrolment menu path, including setting up core auto enrolment parameters, pay code options, pay group options, pension scheme options, state pension ages, earnings parameters, pension rules, and company parameters. The document explains what auto enrolment is—a legal requirement for UK employers to automatically enroll eligible employees into workplace pension schemes—and defines eligibility criteria based on age (22 to State Pension Age), earnings thresholds, and UK employment status. Within the main Auto Enrolment configuration screen, administrators configure critical fields such as Staging Period, Auto Enrolment Min Age, Auto Enrolment Max Age, Minimum Eligible Jobholder Age, Re Enrolment Years, Default Pension Scheme, and optional settings like Multipost Aggregate Earnings and Postpone Pension Enrolment based on Employee Start Date. The guide details how to configure pay codes by marking non-qualifying earnings types (including negative allowances) to exclude them from eligibility calculations, and how to exclude specific pay groups for multi-country organizations. Payroll administrators and HR configuration specialists use this document to ensure their system correctly implements UK auto enrolment legislation, manages employee pension contributions, handles opt-outs, and manages three-year re-enrolment cycles. The document includes cross-references to external resources such as the Pension Regulator website to verify whether existing pension schemes meet auto enrolment requirements.

f: PeopleXD Payroll- Configuring Statutory Payments (UK) V1.0.pdf
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure Payroll to manage statutory payments. Statutory payments are payments that are made to employees to cover earnings lost when they are absent from work either through illness or because they are becoming a parent. Payments covered include: • Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) • Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP) • Additional Statutory Paternity Pay (ASPP) • Ordinary Statutory Sick Pay (OSSP)
ss: Configure statutory payment types in PeopleXD Payroll including Statutory Sick Pay (SSP), Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP), Adoption Pay (SAP), and redundancy payments for UK employees. This guide walks you through setting up SSP rates, granting user access to configuration screens, and defining parameters for each statutory payment type such as qualifying days, waiting periods, and recovery rules. Open this document when you need to establish or update how your payroll system calculates and processes statutory payments for employee absences, parental leave, or redundancy scenarios.
sl: This PeopleXD Payroll user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring statutory payments within the UK payroll system, covering processes for Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP), Statutory Adoption Pay (SAP), Statutory Sick Pay (SSP), Shared Parental Leave, and Redundancy. The document explains how to configure SSP rates by navigating to Settings > UK Tax Rates > Maintain SSP Rates, where users can view pre-configured annual rates, edit existing rates, and add new rate types with associated weekly rates and limits using the blue Add button and green Save button. sl: This document is a user guide for the Payscale Restriction Matrix feature within PeopleXD's CoreHR system, designed to help HR administrators control which pay scales are available when creating or modifying employee salary records. The configuration process involves clicking the Add New button on the Payscale Restriction Matrix screen to open the Payscale Restriction Setup screen, where administrators select a Reference Type and Reference Item (for example, Country = UK), optionally add a second reference attribute, and then drag and drop applicable pay scales from the Available list to the Assigned list before saving. The guide provides instructions for editing existing rules by selecting the Edit option, making rules active or inactive through multiple options, and deleting rules entirely. A critical consideration emphasized throughout is that all possible employee scenarios must be accounted for in the matrix rules, because if an employee's record does not match any defined rule, no pay scales will be available for selection, potentially blocking salary creation across all CoreHR screens including the New Hire, Replace Contract, Additional Contract, Rehire wizards, and the Amend Salary screen. The guide addresses common workforce scheduling challenges, including identifying and filling uncovered shifts through manual assignment or AutoRoster functionality, with instructions for running the AutoRoster feature, clearing AutoRoster data, reviewing the AutoRoster Log, and managing AutoRoster breaks. Additional sections cover configuring and interpreting Statistics displays, managing the Roster Dashboard, transferring employees to different team areas, and publishing uncovered shifts to relevant staff. This guide is intended for CoreHR administrators and workforce management personnel responsible for daily roster administration, scheduling decisions, and managing shift coverage within an organization.

t: WFM v28_Additional Validation User Guide V28 Customer v1.0
f: WFM v28_Additional Validation User Guide V28 Customer v1.0.pdf
s: Purpose of Guide The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Additional Validation functionality in Time and Attendance, and how this is used. This includes: • What is Additional Validation and when is it used? • Detailed guidance on how to configure each type of Additional Validation. Additional Validation Overview It is possible to configure and use 3 types of Additional Validation within the system.
ss: WFM v28 Additional Validation covers three types of validation rules in the Time and Attendance system designed to prevent unauthorized annual leave cashouts: Max Daily Pay Code Limit, Max Overall Daily Pay Code Limit, and Holidays & Contracted Hours Check. The guide provides detailed configuration steps for each validation type, including how to set maximum hour thresholds on individual pay codes, create validation rules across multiple pay codes, and configure warning or stop alerts across timesheet input, leave approval, and sign-off screens. Open this document when you need to set up or troubleshoot daily hour limits on annual leave pay codes, configure multi-pay-code daily maximums, or ensure weekly leave hours don't exceed contracted hours.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive documentation for the Additional Validation functionality in CoreHR's Time and Attendance v28 system, which is designed to prevent improper cashing out of annual leave for employees. The document covers three distinct types of additional validation: Max Daily Pay Code Limit (a pay code setting that restricts hours entered on a single pay code per day), Max Overall Daily Pay Code Limit (a validation rule that caps total hours across multiple pay codes daily), and Holidays & Contracted Hours Check (a validation rule ensuring weekly hours with annual leave do not exceed contracted hours). Configuration guidance is provided for each validation type, including detailed steps for pay code setup, advance options configuration, rule creation, and assignment of validation rules to companies and work groups. These validations are applied across multiple Time and Attendance screens including Timesheet Input, Time Exceptions, Leave Approval, Absence Details, and Approve/Sign Off, with configurable alert levels set to either warn users or stop transaction processing. The guide includes practical examples such as preventing employees from entering more than 8 hours of annual leave in a single day or restricting meal allowances to €10 per day, and explains how validation can be applied either per day or per individual entry within a day through Advanced Options configuration. This document is intended for system administrators and HR professionals responsible for configuring time and attendance validation rules to enforce organizational leave policies.

t: WFM v28_Advance Period Configuration Guide
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this guide is to show how to advance a period for company and user defined calendars. This screen was previously in the Back Office and has now been brought out to Portal. Administrators are now able to: • Advance the Time and Attendance calendar period on Portal. • Gain access to the company calendar once they choose a specific System User Option .
ss: Advance Period Configuration in WFM v28 allows administrators to move Time and Attendance calendar periods forward on Portal through the Advance Period Screen, which was previously available only in Back Office. Administrators can grant users access to advance calendars at either their home company level or across all companies, and the system displays linked exceptions such as unconfirmed hours, unapproved leave requests, and unapproved pay codes before allowing the period update. Open this guide when you need to set up administrator access to calendar period advancement, configure System User Options for Portal access, or understand how to manage calendar exceptions during the period transition process.
sl: This WFM v28 guide explains how to configure and use the Advance Period functionality for managing Time and Attendance calendar periods in the Workforce Management system, a feature that has been migrated from the Back Office to Portal. Administrators configure access through the Back Office by navigating to System Users and selecting either "Home" (to advance calendars for their home company and associated user-defined calendars) or "All Companies" (to advance periods across all companies and their calendars) under the Generate Timesheets tab. The Advance Period screen on the Administrator Dashboard allows users to select a specific calendar and advance it to the next period by clicking the Update Period button, while simultaneously displaying any associated exceptions at the bottom of the screen. The system identifies three types of exceptions for the current open period: Unconfirmed Hours, Unapproved Leave Requests, and Unapproved Pay Code Exist, and prompts administrators with a warning if exceptions exist before allowing the period advancement to proceed. The configuration requires several specific menu options to function properly, including Advance Period Screen, Companies Calendars (Shifts > Get companies calendars), Update Company Calendar (Shifts > Update companies calendars period), Company Exceptions (Shifts > Get companies exceptions), and Transfer Access controls (Advance Period - Transfer Access and Shifts > Get companies transferaccess). The guide also notes that balance recalculation is no longer performed as part of the advance period process, and administrators can view transferred access hours through the Transferred Access screen controlled by the menu option Advance Period - Transfer Access.

t: WFM V28_Balances User Guide
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this guide is to explain the Balance Screens which have moved from Back Office to Portal. The Balances Screen in Portal removes the need for Administrators to complete the daily balances tasks in the back office. This guide covers the following: • Balance Recalculation • Activate Balances 1.2.
ss: The WFM Balances feature in Portal allows administrators to manage balance recalculation and activation tasks that previously required back office access. This guide covers how to access the Balance Maintenance screen, recalculate balances for individual employees or groups based on your access level (Structure Code, System User, or Team Area), and activate balances within the system. You would use this guide when you need to recalculate balance values or booked values for employees, troubleshoot errors that occur during recalculation, or activate balances in Portal instead of the legacy back office system.
sl: This user guide explains how to use the Balances screens in Workforce Management (WFM) Portal, which have been migrated from the Back Office system to streamline daily balance administration tasks. The guide covers two primary processes: Balance Recalculation and Balance Activation, both accessible through the Quick Jump to WFM Admin Dashboard by selecting Balance Maintenance, which displays all system balances with details including Code, Name, Period, Flexitime Indicator, and Balance Type. The Balance Recalculation section details how administrators can recalculate balances for individual employees or groups by selecting a period from a dropdown, choosing between Balance Values, Booked Values, or Both, and executing the recalculation—with access controlled by Structure Code Access, System User Access, or Team Area Access based on user permissions. The guide explains that during recalculation, the system displays progress status and prevents duplicate recalculations by warning users when a process is already in progress, and provides an Errors Screen (accessed via the Errors button) for addressing any issues that arise. Configuration and integration with the system is managed through specific menu options and web services, including Balance Maintenance (57190473), Balance Recalculation (961177288), and various Roster-related services for retrieving user departments, workgroups, and balance settings. This document is intended for WFM administrators responsible for daily balance maintenance who need to understand the Portal-based workflow as an alternative to Back Office procedures.

t: WFM v28_Calculate Hours Configuration V1.0
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this guide is to explain the Calculate Hours screen. Previously this screen was available in the back office only and has now been brought out to Portal. The screen allows users to calculate both future calculation and real time calculation for selected employees.
ss: The WFM v28 Calculate Hours screen enables workforce managers to process and analyze employee hours through future or real-time calculations, with access controlled by user role (Generate Timesheets, HR Admin, or Team Area permissions). Open this guide when you need to configure the Calculate Hours functionality in your WFM system, understand how to run calculations for individual employees or work groups, or set up the required menu options and security permissions. The guide covers calculation types, employee-level processing, history tracking, and the ability to unlock and recalculate future days after manual entries.
sl: This configuration guide explains the Calculate Hours screen in WFM v28, a feature that has been migrated from back office to Portal to allow users to calculate both future and real-time hours for selected employees. The Calculate Hours screen displays a summary of processed and unprocessed employees, any errors encountered, and the status of calculation runs, with toggles for "Run for Person," "Future Calculation," and "Real Time Calculation" to control calculation parameters. The document outlines three distinct calculation scenarios based on user access types: System Users with Generate Timesheets option (who can select by Company, Work Group, and Employee), HR Admin Access users (who select from a list of employees), and Team Area Access users (whose calculations run based on team area structure). Key configuration menu options required for setup include Core Portal Calculate Hours, Get Hours Calculation, Create Hours Calculation, Calculation Errors, and related menu paths under Shifts such as Get hours calculation, Create hours calculation unlockdays, Get Workgroups, and Get Companies. The History screen tracks calculation details including username, person, work group ranges, run dates, number of employees processed, run time, and calculation status, while the Unlock Days feature allows users to recalculate future days and delete any manual entries associated with those days. This guide is designed for administrators and system users responsible for configuring and maintaining the hours calculation functionality in their workforce management system.

Open this guide when you need to configure how calendar data appears in your WFM system, set up pay code visibility by user role, or learn how to access and navigate employee calendar features. It's essential for WFM administrators and managers who control calendar display settings and for anyone needing step-by-step instructions on calendar configuration and employee calendar screen operations.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive documentation for the Employee Calendars functionality within the Workforce Management (WFM) v28 system that has been made available on the Portal interface. The guide covers two primary screens: the Calendar Configuration Screen and the Employee Calendar Screen, with detailed instructions on accessing each through the WFM Dashboard by selecting WFM Configuration and then Calendar Configuration. The Calendar Configuration Screen allows administrators to customize global calendar settings including the calendar start day, rolling versus fixed month options, month offset for viewing previous periods, and colour assignments for shifts, action-required items, and company events. Users can configure pay code visibility and display properties through separate toggles for Admin, Manager, and Employee access levels, along with settings for colour differentiation, order priority, calendar codes (three-letter identifiers), and highlight options for specific pay codes. The guide addresses control of edit and delete options, management of absences and leave requests, handling of recurring absences, and functionality for rolling back weeks and viewing historical hours data. This document is intended for WFM system administrators, managers, and employees who need to set up calendar configurations, manage pay code visibility across different user roles, and work with absence and shift scheduling features within their organization's workforce management system.

t: WFM v28_Generate Timesheets Parallel Run Configuration V1.0
f: WFM v28_Generate Timesheets Parallel Run Configuration V1.0.pdf
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this guide is to help users configure the Generate Timesheets Parallel Run facility. Parallel Run allows users to report on the parallel tables and to review or report where differences may have occurred in the transferring of hours for a previously completed back office Live Run. By using the Parallel Ru n, you can compare to existing Live runs completed through back office and ensure there are no errors before migrating to live...
ss: WFM v28's Generate Timesheets Parallel Run allows you to configure and test timesheet generation in a safe mode before going live with the Portal version, comparing results against your existing back office Live Runs to catch any errors. This feature is especially valuable when migrating from back office timesheet processing to Portal or when transferring large volumes of hours to payroll, as it stores parallel data for detailed review without affecting live operations. Open this guide when you're setting up parallel mode configuration, need to verify your migration process, or want to compare employee hours and payroll details between parallel and live runs before final transfer. The document walks through all nine steps of the parallel run process, from initial generation through final reporting and controls.
sl: This configuration guide provides comprehensive instructions for setting up and executing the Generate Timesheets Parallel Run facility within Workforce Management v28, enabling users to validate the migration of timesheet processing from back office to Portal before going live. The document walks through nine sequential steps spanning sections 2.1.1 through 2.1.9, beginning with accessing the Generate Timesheets Screen on Portal, running the process in Back Office, reviewing Portal Screen Periods and Company Display, transferring hours, and culminating in Parallel Run Reporting to verify no discrepancies exist. Parallel Run allows organizations to compare current Portal-generated results against previously completed back office Live Runs, making it particularly valuable for sites processing large volumes of hours, as it creates a safety mechanism to identify errors before fully migrating to Portal-based operations. The guide covers specific configuration elements including menu access paths, dashboard navigation, controls and tables used for parallel processing, and enhanced features such as Basic Rule functionality with user-defined calendars, amended Employee not on Payroll blocker exceptions, and balance recalculation for departing staff. Key benefits highlighted include verification of the migration process, employee and hours visibility before payroll transfer, continuous system feedback with estimated process duration and completion notifications, background task-list processing that frees administrative resources, and the ability to view generated payroll hours details prior to transfer. This document is designed for workforce management administrators and payroll specialists implementing the transition from back office to Portal-based timesheet generation, particularly those managing complex multi-company environments where Parallel Run can be enabled separately per WFM company without impacting live mode operations.

sl: This configuration guide provides instructions for setting up and using the Generate Timesheets Parallel Run facility within Workforce Management (WFM) Version 28, which has transitioned the Generate Timesheets process from back office to Portal. t: WFM v28_Generate Timesheets User Guide
s: The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to generate timesheets. This functionality for generating timesheets was previously completed through the Back Office and is now available on CorePortal. This is a brand new CoreHR feature for V28.
ss: The Generate Timesheets feature in WFM V28 converts Time & Attendance (T&A) timesheets into Payroll Hours based on configured payroll rules, then transfers those hours to CoreHR Payroll or creates an interface file. This functionality has moved from the Back Office to CorePortal, allowing you to retrieve hours, view converted payroll details before transfer, and manage the process from either the Workforce Management or Admin Dashboard. Open this guide when you need to retrieve employee hours for payroll processing, transfer hours to the payroll system, approve or reject timesheet hours, or troubleshoot errors in the timesheet generation process. The guide also covers configuration settings for supervisor enquiry screens and special handling for employees who are leavers or not on payroll.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for the WFM v28 Generate Timesheets functionality, a new feature in CoreHR v28 that migrates timesheet generation from the Back Office to CorePortal access via the Workforce Management Dashboard or Admin Dashboard. The document covers the two-step Generate Timesheets process: Step 1 (Ready to Retrieve) converts Time & Attendance timesheets into Payroll Hours based on configured payroll rules, and Step 2 (Ready to Transfer) transfers those Payroll Hours to CoreHR Payroll or creates an interface file. Users access the main Generate Timesheets screen by Quick Jumping to the Workforce Management section, where they can select specific calendars by company, view relevant columns such as T&A Company, Calendar name, Period Date, Period Code, Stage, and Status, and choose to run the process for all workgroups (Select All) or a specific range (Select Range). The guide addresses common errors and problems that may occur during the Retrieve Hours process through a dedicated error table and troubleshooting section, while also detailing related screens including Employees to be Transferred, Payroll Hours, and View History, as well as approval workflows through functions like Approve Hours, Reject Hours, and Add/View Comments. Configuration requirements are documented in Section 5, covering General Configuration, CorePortal access setup, Supervisor Enquiry screen configuration with Contact Type settings, and special handling for employee leavers and employees not on payroll. This guide is primarily used by payroll administrators, supervisors, and workforce management personnel who need to process timesheets, approve hours, and manage the integration between Time & Attendance and Payroll systems.

t: WFM v28_Leave Requests and Absences User Guide v1.0
f: WFM v28_Leave Requests and Absences User Guide v1.0.pdf
s: Purpose of Document The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Leave Requests and Absences functionality in Time and Attendance, and how this is used. What are Leave Requests and Absences?
ss: Leave Requests and Absences covers the end-to-end process for submitting, approving, and managing employee time off in CoreHR's Time & Attendance system. It walks through how employees submit and track leave requests, how managers approve or reject them, and how administrators set up leave types, balances, and entitlements. Open this guide if you need to understand leave workflows, configure absence management, check your leave balance, or learn how to approve team leave requests. This applies to anyone using CoreHR's self-service features for leave management, from individual contributors to HR administrators.
sl: This comprehensive user guide for WFM v28 covers the complete management of leave requests and absences within the CoreHR system, providing detailed instructions for employees, managers, and administrators across multiple functional areas. The document explains fundamental concepts including leave types, balance management, and the distinction between leave requests and absences, while outlining the leave request workflow that governs how requests move through the system. For employee balance management, the guide details how to access the Balance Overview Screen, manage balance assignments, and utilize various balance options including Edit Set-up, Entitlement Basis, Re-calculate, Balance Adjustment, and Deactivate/Reactivate functions found in section 2. Employee Self Service functionality is extensively documented, covering how users can view balances through widgets, submit standard and part-day leave requests, upload supporting documents, and manage their requests through screens such as the Calendar Board, Work Week view, and My Requests section. Manager Self Service capabilities include approving or rejecting leave requests via the Notification Centre and My Approvals Notifications Widget, viewing team balances on the Team Balances Screen, and entering or managing employee absences through the Team Scheduler and Roster Details screens. The guide also addresses configuration aspects for system administrators, including Balance Type Driving Parameters with three variations (Auto Derived Entitlement, Maintain Only Balance, and Other Balances), HR Process Task List setup, CorePortal Balance System Parameters, and the prerequisites for enabling leave request functionality with appropriate organisation roles and system parameters. This document serves employees, managers, and HR administrators who need to understand or implement leave and absence management processes within the CoreHR workforce management system.

t: WFM v28_Overlapping Leave and Absence Requests User Guide 1.0v
f: WFM v28_Overlapping Leave and Absence Requests User Guide 1.0v.pdf
s: Purpose of Document The purpose of this guide is to provide an overview of user guidance and the configuration associated with the Overlapping Warnings feature. Items covered include: • Overlapping warnings configuration • Dashboard configuration • Security configuration • Viewing overlapping warnings 1.2. Overview of Feature Overlapping Warnings display during the actioning of employee Leave Requests, alerting the approver at the approval/rejection stage.
ss: WFM Time v28's Overlapping Warnings feature alerts approvers when a leave or absence request conflicts with other employees' absences, pending requests, or previously rejected requests for the same employee. This guide covers how to configure the warnings globally through the Absence Warning Configuration screen, set up the necessary dashboard widgets and security access, and interpret the different types of overlap warnings when approving requests. Open this document if you need to enable or customize overlap warnings for your team's leave approval process, or if you want to understand what warning scenarios will appear during leave request approvals.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive documentation for the Overlapping Warnings feature within the WFM Time v28 system, specifically for CoreHR Limited's workforce management platform. The guide covers the full lifecycle of the feature including how to configure overlapping warnings, set up dashboard access, establish security permissions, and interpret warning displays when approvers action leave requests. The configuration process involves accessing the Absence Warning Configuration screen through the Time and Attendance Settings widget on the Administrator Dashboard, requiring users to first add the widget and then configure the applicable Menu Options (CorePortal – Time and Attendance Settings and Absence Warning Configuration) within their Menu Profile for proper access. The warnings system alerts approvers during the leave request approval/rejection stage when a request overlaps with rejected requests for the same employee, team absences, unapproved team requests, or combinations thereof, as detailed through five specific configuration indicators controlling Rejected Request Overlap, Different Absence Type/Pay Code filtering, Absence Types/Pay Codes scope, Team Absence Overlap, and Unactioned Request Overlap scenarios. System administrators and approvers use this document to understand how to enable or disable warnings globally across all users (not individual profiles), configure which leave types trigger warnings through Personalised Pay Code Groups, and interpret the various overlapping warning examples provided for rejected requests, team absences, and team requests. It is important to note that warnings function as informational alerts only and do not prevent approvers from approving or rejecting requests, and sick absence warnings only display when submitted through the approval process rather than when directly entered on employee records.

t: WFM v28_Pay Code Access Groups Configuration V1.0

You'd open this document if you need to set up customized pay code lists, manage which codes managers can input versus view-only, or configure pay code access by employee appointment or work group. It's essential for organizations that want to limit pay code visibility based on role or employment type.
sl: This document is a comprehensive configuration guide for WFM v28's Pay Code Access Groups functionality, designed specifically for HR Administrators who manage the pay codes available to managers and employees across leave requests, absences, and timesheets. The guide covers the complete workflow for creating, amending, and deleting pay code groups, with step-by-step instructions for accessing these functions either through the Manage Pay Code Group screen via People Management or through the WFM Configuration Data Centre by navigating to Administrator Dashboard > WFM Dashboard Config > Configuration Settings > Pay Code Groups. Pay Code Groups enable administrators to tailor which pay codes are displayed to employees and managers during data entry, with version 28 introducing the ability to link manager absence and timesheet entries to pay code groups assigned at the employee and appointment level. This guide is essential for administrators implementing access controls across multiple WFM screens including Timesheet Input, Absence Details, Time Exceptions, and back-office functions like Record Absence Details and Maintain Hours.

t: WFM V28_Pro Rata Length of Service Increments v1.0
f: WFM V28_Pro Rata Length of Service Increments v1.0.pdf
s: Purpose of Guide The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Pro Rata Length of Service Increments functionality in Time and Attendance, and how this is used. This includes: • What is Pro Rata Length of Service Increments and when is it used? • Detailed guidance on the configuration options within Pro Rata Length of Service Increments. What is Pro Rata Length of Service Increments?
ss: Pro Rata Length of Service Increments in WFM v28 enables you to calculate anniversary-based service increment awards on a proportional basis, adjusting for partial years worked based on dates, weeks, or months. Open this guide if you need to configure how length of service increments are awarded to employees, particularly part-time or full-time staff who don't complete a full service year before their anniversary date. The document provides step-by-step configuration instructions via the Balance Parameters screen in CoreTime/CoreRoster, along with worked examples showing calculations for different employee types. Use this when setting up or troubleshooting service increment entitlements that account for employee FTE levels and varying calculation periods.
sl: This user guide for WFM V28 Pro Rata Length of Service Increments explains how the Time and Attendance system handles pro-rata anniversary-based length of service increments, which allows organizations to calculate service increment awards based on the portion of the year an employee has worked rather than awarding the full increment. The functionality is configured through the Balance Parameters screen (accessed via Backoffice > CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Params > Balances > Parameters), where users enter a balance code and select the Length of Service section to access configuration options. The pro-rata calculation can be based on dates, weeks, or months between an employee's anniversary date and the end of the annual leave year, taking into account the employee's FTE (full-time equivalent) and applying rounding rules at the balance level. This feature is only applicable when the Length of Service – Calculate On parameter is set to either Anniversary (which uses the personnel master start date and ignores contract history) or Post Appointment Anniversary (which considers contract history and enables additional options like Use Service in Company and Exclude Leave for service breaks). The Anniversary Pro-Rata (Override) section on the Balance Parameters screen contains key fields such as Apply FTE to Service Increment (set to Current Appointment to capture the employee's FTE at their anniversary date) and Pro-Rata prior to Anniversary date (which defaults to dates but can be set to weeks or months). The guide includes five worked examples demonstrating how these calculations apply to both full-time and part-time employees across different calculation bases, and it accounts for scenarios where employees are leaving the organization, which impacts their service increment entitlements.

t: WFM V28_Sign Off Hours User Guide
f: WFM V28_Sign Off Hours User Guide.pdf
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this guide is to outline the screens in Portal which have moved from the Back Office for signing off hours. The Sign-off Hours screen gives you a sign-off facility, which is a final confirmation that all hours and are correct for the current period. This means that the hours are correct and approved and that the current WFM period can be completed.
ss: The Sign Off Hours screen in WFM allows managers and admins to review, approve, and finalize employee hours before they're transferred to payroll for a given period. It organizes hours into four tabs—Action Required, Pending Sign Off, Signed Off, and Rejected—so you can track which employees need attention, which are ready to be approved, which have been completed, and which have been rejected. You can sign off hours individually or in bulk (up to 100 records at a time), and you can search by employee, filter by workgroup, or view detailed timesheets for any discrepancies. Open this guide when you need to learn how to navigate the Sign Off Hours screen, understand what each tab shows, or perform bulk sign-off operations.
sl: This user guide provides a comprehensive overview of the Sign Off Hours screen in WFM V28, which has been migrated from the Back Office to Portal and serves as a final confirmation mechanism for approving hours before payroll transfer. The document explains how to access the Sign Off Hours screen by navigating through the WFM Admin Dashboard and selecting Sign Off Hours from the left-hand menu, with the option to select between calendars and search for specific employees using the Search Employees field at the top left. The guide details four main tabs that organize workflow: Action Required (flagging hours needing attention), Pending Sign Off (showing approved hours awaiting manager or admin sign-off), Signed Off (displaying already-approved hours), and Rejected (showing hours rejected and held from payroll release). Users can sign off hours individually by clicking the action button next to each employee or use the Bulk Sign Off feature to process up to 100 records simultaneously using the Select All button, with options to Sign Off, Reject, or View Timesheet for each entry. The screen displays key fields including Team Member Name, Post Title, Rostered Hours, and Differences (configured differences between hours totals and contact hours, rostered hours, or payroll hours). Managers and administrators can customize the position of the Sign Off Hours menu option on their respective dashboards through the WFM Configuration Centre by selecting Dashboard Configuration and entering a position number such as #3. This guide is essential for managers and administrators who need to approve and finalize employee hours at the end of each WFM period before hours are transferred to payroll.

t: WFM v28_Workgroups User Guide

The Work Group configuration screen is now available via Portal on the WFM Admin Dashboard and replaces the back office Work Group Configuration Screen. ss: WFM v28 Workgroups covers how to set up and manage work groups within the Workforce Management system via the WFM Admin Dashboard Portal. It walks through creating new workgroups, configuring payment rules, payroll hours, absence handling, trigger points, and other advanced settings that control how employee time and attendance data are processed. Open this guide when you need to establish workgroup parameters, modify existing workgroup configurations, or understand the various tabs and screens available for workgroup management. You'll also find instructions on searching, filtering, copying, and deactivating workgroups from the landing page.
sl: This guide introduces the Work Groups feature in WFM v28, which is accessed through the WFM Admin Dashboard via Portal and replaces the legacy back office Work Group Configuration Screen. The document covers the Work Group landing page and eight associated configuration screens: General Parameters, Payment Rules, Default Payroll Hours, Group Codes, Trigger Points, Extra Hours Recoding, Absence Contract Days, and Advanced Config, each containing specific settings for workforce management. To access the Work Groups screen, users navigate through Quick Jump to WFM Admin Dashboard, then select WFM Configuration followed by Work Groups, requiring activation of the menu option workgroup_config_access and three webservices (Update Settings, Get Settings, and Create Settings under Roster). The Work Group landing page displays a searchable and filterable grid showing all active work groups with editable fields including Work Group Code, Work Group Name, Company, and Holiday Scheme, allowing users to search by free text or restrict results using filters on key fields. The guide enables administrators to perform core workgroup management tasks including marking workgroups inactive, adding new workgroups, copying existing configurations, and deleting workgroups. This document is primarily used by Workforce Management administrators and configuration specialists who need to set up, modify, and maintain workgroup settings that control payroll rules, payment thresholds, absence policies, and other HR system parameters.

The roster section describes multiple operational processes such as cost analysis, day and week view displays showing rostered times and employee working or resting status, roster change tracking, team area access assignment, and uncovered shift publishing functionality. ss: CoreHESA is a module within CoreHR that enables higher education institutions to create, maintain, and submit HESA (Higher Education Statistics Agency) records for UK reporting requirements. This guide covers configuring the CoreHESA system—including user access, staff and contract record setup, data mapping rules, and custom fields—as well as the complete generation process from initial data creation through XML file production. You'll use this guide when setting up CoreHESA for the first time, generating annual HESA submissions, making data corrections and bulk uploads, or performing year-end rollover procedures. Open it if you need step-by-step instructions on validating HESA data, troubleshooting mapping issues, or understanding business rule validation requirements.
sl: The XD HESA User Guide is a comprehensive manual for configuring and using the CoreHESA module, which enables higher education institutions in the UK to create, maintain, and submit HESA (Higher Education Statistics Agency) records and generate XML returns for regulatory compliance. The document covers initial setup and configuration tasks including user access management through CoreHESA Menu Options and CoreHESA User Security settings, as well as system parameter configuration and staff and contract record setup through field parameters, data mapping rules, and mapping references. It provides detailed instructions on mapping PeopleXD pay scale points to CoreHESA framework points, configuring allowances, and setting up HESA User-Defined Fields (UDFs) that can be updated via the Employee Self Service portal or back office, along with guidance on configuring exemptions and generating HESA Staff IDs. The guide describes the complete CoreHESA generation process, including creating initial data sets, using the HESA Mapping Engine and HESA Tracker Log, and performing manual corrections or bulk data uploads through multiple options for person values, contract values, UDF values, and contract exclusions. It addresses critical validation and error resolution through business rules validation that can be run during initial data set generation or as a standalone task, with reporting capabilities to identify issues before XML generation. The document also includes year-end processes such as generating XML files and performing the HESA new year rollover, which involves copying configuration and rolling over the HESA year with confirmation steps. This guide is essential for HESA administrators, HR system managers, and IT personnel responsible for higher education institution compliance reporting who need to understand both configuration requirements and operational tasks for producing valid HESA returns.

ss: The Applicant One View feature in XD Recruitment provides recruitment administrators with a centralized view to manage candidate information throughout the hiring process. Open this guide when you need to understand how to navigate candidate records, track applicant progress through interview and offer stages, or configure which applicant information is visible to your team in the People XD Applicant Tracking System.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive documentation for the Applicant One View feature within the XD Recruitment system, which is integrated with the People XD Applicant Tracking System and Volcanic platform. The document explains how recruitment administrators can access and utilize a centralized dashboard to view and update candidate information across multiple data categories including applicant personal details, vacancy and application information, correspondence, references, events, documents, diversity details, and user-defined fields.
