t: Personnel Number Generation
s:
# Summary of Personnel Number Generation Guide

This guide teaches users how to configure the PeopleXD CoreHR system to manage how employee personnel numbers are created or assigned when setting up new employees.

## What You'll Learn

**Two Personnel Number Generation Options:**

1. **Automatic Generation** — The system automatically creates a personnel number for each new hire based on configurable rules. Numbers can be customized to match your organization's requirements, including adding prefixes, suffixes, and controlling the number length.

2. **Manual Generation** — Personnel numbers must be manually entered into the system for each new hire, with no automatic format validation.

The system can be configured to use either option exclusively, or both options can be active simultaneously, allowing users to choose which method to use when creating each new employee record.

## Configuration Steps

The guide walks through:
- Where to access personnel number configuration settings in the system (via the Data Centre widget and HR Admin Setup)
- How to define and activate generation rules for automatic numbering
- How to set the system parameter to either automatic or manual mode
- How to use the Create New Employee Wizard with your chosen method
- Additional technical considerations including valid format indicators and modulus generation routines

By following this guide, users will be able to set up personnel number generation according to their organization's employee numbering policies and requirements.

t: Post Restructuring
s:
# Post Restructuring Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to use the Post Restructuring functionality in PeopleXD to reorganise the company's structure—either consolidating business units or creating new ones.

## Key Learning Outcomes

After reading this guide, users will understand:

**What a Restructuring Profile is:** A container holding all details needed for an organisational move, including the old and new post structure, effective date, and affected employees. Multiple profiles can be created and edited until processed, after which they're locked.

**The complete post-restructuring process**, which involves 12 sequential steps:

1. Remove any confirmed future appointments and outstanding salary approvals that would interfere with the restructuring
2. Add new reference data (new departments, sections, or posts) to the system
3. Link new reference data items to the organisational hierarchy tree
4. Grant system users access to any newly created departments
5. Create the required restructuring profile(s)—one profile per unique employee movement
6. View affected employees and run validation checks
7. Identify and fix any errors found during validation
8. Generate a report showing the changes
9. Process the transfer to apply changes
10. Request PeopleXD to synchronise system tables
11. Run the report again and save it locally
12. Perform spot checks on employees to verify the restructuring worked correctly

**Important constraints:** Users learn that restructuring only updates the post hierarchy (department, section, etc.), creates a new sequence in the appointment record without changing the employee ID, doesn't affect salary or allowances, must be tested on UAT before running on Live, and only processes the most recent active appointment.

t: Probation Dates
s:
# Summary: Probation Dates User Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators how to manage and record probation information for employees in the PeopleXD HR system (CoreHR). 

**Key learning outcomes:**

After reading this guide, users will understand how to:

- **Record probation expiry dates** — the planned end date of an employee's probation period (e.g., 6 months after hire)
- **Capture probation review dates** — track up to two review points during the probation period
- **Document probation extensions** — record when probation periods are extended

**Two methods are covered:**

1. **Direct input** — HR administrators can manually enter probation details directly onto an employee's contract record
2. **Automated setup via Terms and Conditions Profiles** — administrators can create standard probation periods (e.g., 6 months) that automatically calculate the expiry date based on the contract start date and can be reused across multiple posts and contracts

**Important context:**

The guide explains that probation information is stored at the contract level (not the employee/person level), meaning different probation periods can be recorded for different contracts an employee may hold, such as initial hiring contracts, promotion contracts, or rehire contracts.

t: Reference Data
s:
# Summary of PeopleXD Reference Data User Guide

This guide teaches users how to work with Reference Data in the PeopleXD People Management system.

**What is Reference Data:**
The guide explains that Reference Data consists of standardized information and codes that are used throughout the HR system to ensure consistent data entry and classification. These are foundational lookup values that populate dropdown menus and categorization fields.

**What You'll Learn:**

1. **Understanding Reference Data Structure** — The guide covers the different types of reference data screens available in PeopleXD, including standard reference data, non-standard reference data, and additional reference data areas used by specific modules (Workforce Management, Talent Management, and Recruitment).

2. **Basic Data Management Operations** — You'll learn how to:
   - Add new reference data entries
   - Edit existing reference data
   - Delete reference data entries

3. **Specific Reference Data Types** — The guide provides detailed information about commonly used reference data categories, including:
   - Job-related data (job title codes, job categories)
   - Employee classifications (employee status, sub-status, categories, sub-categories)
   - Operational data (FTE hours, action codes, project codes)
   - Reason codes for various HR transactions

4. **Advanced Configuration** — Users learn how to configure reason codes with specific features such as restricting lists based on criteria, toggling between contract and salary applications, and setting up questionnaire profiles.

After reading this guide, users will be able to navigate and manage the reference data that underpins their organization's HR information in PeopleXD.

t: Rehires
s:
# Rehires Guide Summary

This guide teaches HR administrators how to rehire former employees who are no longer active in the PeopleXD system. Here's what you'll learn:

## Key Capabilities

**Understanding Rehires:**
- You can only rehire employees whose previous employment was already recorded in the system and who are currently marked as "dormant" (inactive)
- When you rehire someone, their existing HR record is reactivated rather than creating a new one
- Their personal information can be updated to reflect any changes since they last worked
- Once rehired and their contract is commenced, they become available to payroll with a new salary

## Step-by-Step Process

The guide walks through the complete **4-step Rehire Person Wizard**:

1. **Person Info** — Review and update the employee's personal details, which may have changed since their previous employment

2. **Organisational Structure** — Select the post (job position) for the new contract, with options for auto-authorised posts or authorised appointments with sequence numbers

3. **Contract Information** — Set up contract details with restrictions (such as the effective date cannot be earlier than their previous leave date)

4. **Commencement** — Finalize and commence the appointment

## Additional Topics

The guide also covers how to identify potential rehires through duplicate employee checks and validation rules for pay group assignments.

t: Salary Approval Configuration
s:
# Summary: Salary Approval Configuration Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators how to set up and manage salary approval processes in the PeopleXD CorePortal system. After reading it, users will understand how to configure two different types of salary approval workflows:

**Standard Salary Approvals** — This approach involves setting up organizational role types and assigning them to employees. Users will learn how to define approval roles (such as managers or supervisors), establish approval groups, determine the sequence in which approvals must occur, and assign these roles to specific employees within the organization. The guide covers role naming conventions, active/inactive status management, and how to grant access to both salary approvers and system administrators.

**Workflow-Based Salary Approvals** — This is a more flexible approach using custom workflow processes. Users will learn why workflow-based approvals are needed, how to configure workflow processes, how to link organizational role types to workflows, and how to assign employee groups to specific approval workflows. This section also covers how to exclude certain employee groups from particular workflows when needed.

**Additional Coverage** — The guide includes information about user access and menu permissions for both salary approvers and administrators, as well as upgrade considerations for organizations transitioning from existing configurations or managing legacy contact types.

In essence, this guide enables HR administrators to establish and manage the rules and processes that determine how salary changes and approvals flow through their organization in the CorePortal system.

t: Salary Approvals
s:
# Salary Approvals Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to use the Salary Approvals feature in the PeopleXD HR system (CoreHR). After reading it, you will understand:

**What Salary Approvals Are:**
- A control mechanism that requires all new salary and allowance records to go through a formal approval process before they can be used by the Payroll system
- Salary records move through different approval statuses: "Pending" (initial state, not available to payroll), "In Approval" (approved by some but not all approvers, still not available to payroll), and "Approved" or "Future" (fully approved and ready for payroll processing)

**Two Approval Methods:**
The system offers two different approaches to managing salary approvals—Standard Salary Approvals and Workflow-Based Salary Approvals.

**How to Navigate and Use the System:**
- Understanding the Salary Approvals screen and its different views (your pending approvals, all outstanding items, rejected items, and historical approval records)
- Viewing the salary request details and employee information
- How to approve or reject outstanding salary and allowance requests
- How different payroll scenarios and employee payroll setup configurations affect approvals
- How to track approval status on the Current Salary screen
- How to delete pending salary records when needed

The guide provides step-by-step instructions for managers and administrators who need to review, approve, or manage salary and allowance changes within the system.

t: Salary Increment Configuration
s:
# Summary of "Salary Increment Configuration" Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators how to set up and configure the salary increment process in the PeopleXD CoreHR system.

After reading this guide, users will understand:

**System Parameters Configuration:**
- How to enable the HR-controlled increment process, which activates the automatic daily increment system
- How to set the "Increment Days" parameter, which determines how far in advance the system searches for upcoming salary increment due dates (for example, setting it to 30 days means the system will identify and process all increments due within the next 30 days)
- How to control whether salary amendments created by the increment process require approval through the standard salary approval workflows, or whether they should bypass approvals and be automatically approved for immediate payroll processing

**User Access Permissions:**
- How to configure which users can view the history of salary increments
- How to grant permissions for users to amend increment details

**System Setup:**
- How to access the necessary HR Admin setup screens and locate the relevant system parameters
- How to run the increment process job

The guide provides practical, step-by-step instructions for configuring these features to support an organization's salary increment workflows, with options to automate the process or require approval depending on business requirements.

t: Salary Increments
s:
# Salary Increments Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to manage salary increments in the PeopleXD HR system, specifically for employees on pay scales.

**What you'll learn:**

The guide explains the automatic increment process, which automatically creates a new salary record that moves an employee to the next point on their pay scale, eliminating the need to manually create salary amendments for regular annual or periodic increases. This can apply to all employees on a common date or to individual employees based on dates specific to their employment (such as 12 months from their start date).

**Key concepts covered:**

- **How increments work** — The system runs daily to identify employees whose increment due date is approaching (typically within a set number of days, like 30 days in advance) and automatically generates the appropriate salary amendment
- **Pay scale requirements** — Increments only apply to employees with "Pay Scale" salaries; they cannot be automatically created for "Personal" rate salaries
- **Increment attributes** — Key terms like "Increment Due Date" (when the increment should be applied) and the "Increment System Job" (the daily automated process)

**Practical tasks you'll be able to perform:**

- View, add, and delete increment due dates
- Generate incremented salary amendments through the daily increment process
- Identify which salaries have been incremented
- Manage increment hold indicators
- Process salary approvals related to increments
- Review increment history records

t: Social Security Settings
s:
# Summary: Social Security Settings Guide

This guide teaches users how to configure and use the Social Security Settings feature in the PeopleXD HR system to manage social security number validation across multiple countries.

## What You'll Learn

**Core Functionality:**
The guide explains that Social Security Settings allows organizations to set up validation rules for employee social security numbers, with built-in support for:
- PPS Numbers (Republic of Ireland)
- NI Numbers (United Kingdom)

**Configuration Capabilities:**
After reading this guide, you'll understand how to:
- Set a default social security number type and validation rule for your organization
- Create exceptions for groups of employees in different jurisdictions that require different validation rules or no validation at all
- Customize field labels to match different countries' social security terminology
- Apply different validation requirements based on employee location or contract details

**Practical Example:**
The guide illustrates how to configure a system that uses NI Number validation by default for UK employees, applies PPS Number validation for employees based in Ireland (identified by their contract location), and allows unrestricted number formats for employees in other countries—with appropriate labels displayed for each group.

**Technical Setup:**
You'll also learn where to access the Social Security Settings feature in the system (via the Data Centre widget and HR Admin Setup), how to configure global settings and exceptions, and what additional parameters need to be enabled to activate the feature.

t: Successful Applicants
s:
# Successful Applicants Guide Summary

This guide teaches HR administrators how to process successful job applicants through the PeopleXD People Management system after they've accepted job offers in the Recruitment module.

## What You'll Learn

**Main Processes Covered:**
- How to access the list of successful applicants waiting to be processed
- How to set up contracts for three types of hires:
  - **New starters** – brand new employees joining the company
  - **New contracts for existing employees** – both replacement contracts (changing roles) and additional contracts (taking on extra positions)
  - **Rehires** – former employees being brought back

**Key Functionality:**
- Navigating to and viewing the Successful Applicants screen, which displays applicants ready for processing
- Understanding which applicants appear on your screen based on your HR access permissions (you'll only see applicants linked to contracts/posts you have access to)
- Reading applicant summary information including their name, applicant number, personnel number, vacancy details, intended start date, and post
- Completing the contract creation process for each applicant type
- Processing the "Commence Appointment" step for new starters
- Managing applicant details on employee records once hired

The guide is designed for HR administrators who use both the Recruitment and People Management modules and need to finalize employment contracts for candidates who have accepted job offers.

t: Task List Configuration
s:
# Task List Configuration Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage HR Process Task Lists in the PeopleXD HR system.

## What You'll Learn:

**Core Concepts:**
- What HR Process Task Lists are and their purpose in the system

**Creating and Managing Task Lists:**
- How to access the HR Task Lists screen
- How to create a new task list from scratch
- How to add individual task list items to your configuration

**Configurable Task Steps:**

The guide covers all the different types of HR-related information steps you can include in a task list, such as:
- **Employment & Access:** User access assignments, leaver access, probation details, terms and conditions (general, pay, and balances)

In essence, this guide enables HR administrators to configure customized checklists of employee information and HR processes that need to be completed for various HR workflows.

t: Terms & Conditions
s:
# PeopleXD Terms & Conditions User Guide — Summary

This guide teaches users how to manage Terms and Conditions (T&C) Profiles in the PeopleXD HR system.

**What you'll learn:**

The guide covers the complete lifecycle of T&C Profiles:

- **Understanding T&C Profiles**: What they are (reusable templates of contracted terms and conditions), what contract elements they contain (probation expiry dates, notice periods, increment dates, allowances, and leave balances), and how they work within the system.

- **Creating and managing profiles**: How to create new T&C Profiles from scratch, set up profile rules to determine when profiles apply based on criteria like employee status or location, configure general settings, pay components, and balance information. The guide also covers how to duplicate existing profiles, update them, and delete them when no longer needed.

- **Assigning T&Cs to contracts**: How to link T&C Profiles to Post Profiles (job templates), assign specific allowances and balances to posts, and apply T&C Profiles to individual employee contracts. This includes handling different contract types such as auto-authorised contracts, auto-commenced contracts, standard contracts, and restructured contracts.

After reading this guide, users will be able to set up standardised terms and conditions templates and apply them consistently across posts and employee contracts in the system.

t: Terms & Conditions Configuration
s:
# Summary: Terms & Conditions Configuration Guide

This guide teaches users how to configure the PeopleXD HR system to use Terms and Conditions Profiles. After reading it, users will understand how to:

**Set Up Access and Permissions:**
- Grant system access to the Terms and Conditions setup functionality through the appropriate menu options in People Management
- Enable user access to manage Terms and Conditions Profiles

**Configure Task Lists:**
- Access and set up HR Task Lists to include Terms and Conditions options
- Enable task lists to appear when completing new hire, contract replacement, or rehire processes
- Add specific Terms and Conditions task list steps to employee workflows, including:
  - Terms and Conditions General (required as a foundation step)
  - Terms and Conditions Balances (requires the General step to also be used)
  - Terms and Conditions Pay (requires the General step to also be used)

**Manage Employee-Level Access:**
- Control how employees access their Terms and Conditions information
- Manage related functions like allowances and balances

The guide is a configuration manual focused on system administration and setup rather than end-user operations. It assumes the user has the ability to manage menu options and access controls within the CoreHR system, and that the actual Terms and Conditions profiles themselves are set up separately using a different guide.

t: User Data Access
s:
# Summary: User Data Access Guide

This guide teaches HR system administrators how to manage and control user access to employee data within the PeopleXD HR system.

Specifically, users will learn how to:

**Understand Access Fundamentals:**
- How user access works in the system overall
- How access is controlled based on organisational structure (departments, teams, hierarchies)
- How access is controlled based on pay groups

**Configure User Access:**
- Where access permissions are granted to individual users
- How to grant HR-related access so users can view and manage employee records, employment contracts, and posts/positions
- How to grant pay-related access so users can view and manage salary and allowance information
- How to assign default menu profiles to users so they see the appropriate options for their role

**Apply Additional Data Controls:**
- How to restrict access to substantive contracts (permanent employment contracts)
- How to control access to confirmed future contracts

**Post Profile Access:**
- What additional security configuration is needed for post profile data access within CoreHR

The guide also includes a detailed appendix with screenshots and visual references showing where these access controls appear on various HR screens (employee records, contracts, posts, salary information, etc.), making it a practical reference for administrators implementing these settings.

t: User Defined Field Configuration
s:
# Summary: User Defined Field Configuration Guide

This guide teaches HR system administrators how to configure and manage User Defined Fields (UDFs) in the PeopleXD HR system.

**What you'll learn:**

- **What UDFs are:** Custom fields that can be added to the HR system to capture organization-specific information beyond standard HR data fields
- **How to access UDF configuration:** Where in the system to find and use the UDF configuration tools
- **How to create new UDFs:** A step-by-step process covering adding UDF codes, configuring data labels, defining field types, and setting optional access controls and date parameters
- **How to update and maintain existing UDFs:** How to edit UDF descriptions, modify existing items, add new items, adjust advanced settings, deactivate UDFs, or delete them completely
- **How to control who sees UDFs:** How different user types (HR administrators, managers, and employees) can access and view UDF data, including how to set reporting and dashboard visibility
- **How to implement security restrictions:** How to configure additional security settings when UDFs contain sensitive information that should only be accessible to certain users

The guide provides practical, hands-on instructions for managing the entire lifecycle of custom fields within the HR system.

t: User Defined Field Data
s:
# Summary of "User Defined Field Data" Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators, employees, and managers how to work with User Defined Fields (UDFs) in the PeopleXD HR system.

**What UDFs are:**
User Defined Fields are custom data fields that store information not covered by the system's standard features. They're organisation-specific and vary between companies. For example, a company might use a UDF to record what equipment has been issued to each employee.

**What you'll learn to do:**

1. **Access UDFs** — Navigate to the User Defined Data screen from an employee's HR record to view any existing custom fields

2. **Search for UDFs** — Use keyword searches to find specific UDFs and switch between different employee contracts to view contract-specific custom data

3. **Add UDFs** — Create new user-defined data entries for employees, including understanding the difference between "Person UDFs" (employee-level data) and "Contract UDFs" (specific to an employment contract)

4. **Edit UDFs** — Update existing custom field data that's already been recorded

5. **Delete UDFs** — Remove custom field entries when no longer needed

The guide also covers access controls, such as UDF Assignment Groups that may restrict who can see or add certain types of custom fields, and security settings that may require special permissions to access sensitive custom data.

t: Wage Warning
s:
# Wage Warning Setup Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to set up and configure wage warning validations in the PeopleXD HR system. 

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

- **Understand wage warnings**: Learn what wage warnings are and how they function within the system, including where wage warning validation is available.

- **Configure three types of wage rates**:
  - **Minimum Wage**: Add, edit, delete, and activate minimum wage rates with sample rates provided
  - **Living Wage**: Add, edit, delete, and activate living wage rates with sample rates provided
  - **Apprentice Wage**: Identify apprentice contracts, then add, edit, delete, and activate apprentice wage rates with sample rates provided

- **Access the wage warning setup area**: Know where to navigate in the system to configure these settings.

- **Enable wage warnings**: Switch on wage warning parameters for each of the three wage types (minimum wage, living wage, and apprentice wage warnings).

- **Understand validation application**: Learn how the system applies wage validation checks and key points to note about the validation process.

- **Complete additional configuration**: Set up menu options and customize warning message text as needed.

In essence, this is a practical setup guide for HR administrators who need to configure the system to automatically flag or warn when employee wages fall below specified minimum, living, or apprentice wage thresholds.

t: Portal
s:
# Summary of "Auto Enrolment in Ireland User Guide"

This guide teaches PeopleXD Payroll users how to manage automatic pension enrolment for employees in Ireland.

**What you'll learn:**

- **What auto enrolment is** — the basics of who gets automatically enrolled in pensions and how contributions work
- **Key compliance requirements** — important deadlines and payment rules you must follow, including three critical rules: using NAERSA to determine eligibility, following AEPN instructions precisely, and understanding how pension pots transfer between providers
- **Employee rights** — what options employees have, including the right to opt out or pause contributions
- **The two-step payroll process** — the new steps you need to add to your regular payroll procedures to handle auto enrolment:
  1. Retrieving AEPN instructions (which tell you what pension actions to take for each employee)
  2. Submitting contribution files to the pension provider
- **Technical implementation** — how to use the six APIs (automated interfaces) provided by PeopleXD to communicate with the pension system and exchange the necessary information

The guide is designed for payroll professionals who need to integrate auto enrolment processes into their existing PeopleXD payroll operations and ensure compliance with Irish pension regulations.

t: Back Office
s:
# Summary of "Auto Enrolment in Ireland" User Guide

This guide teaches users how to manage **Auto Enrolment pension processes in Ireland using the PeopleXD Payroll system**.

## What You'll Learn:

**Understanding Auto Enrolment Fundamentals:**
- What auto enrolment is and who it applies to
- How employee contributions work
- Key deadlines and payment rules that must be followed
- The three core rules governing auto enrolment (eligibility determination, following instructions, and pot portability)
- Employee rights, including opting out and pausing contributions
- The legal framework underpinning the scheme

**Integrating Auto Enrolment into Your Payroll:**
- The two essential new steps to add to your standard payroll process
- How to retrieve AEPN (Auto Enrolment Processing Notification) instructions and when to do so
- How to prepare and submit contribution files to the scheme
- What happens at each stage of the process

# Summary

This guide explains how to set up and use the PeopleXD HR system to include National Insurance (NI) savings from salary sacrifice schemes as a pension top-up in budget forecasts.

**What you'll learn:**

- **The purpose**: How to configure the system so that when employees use salary sacrifice for pension contributions, the employer's NI savings are automatically added to the pension top-up amount shown in budget forecasts.

- **Configuration steps**: You need to set up three things in CorePay:
  1. Identify which pay codes are salary sacrifice pay codes and link them to the relevant pension scheme
  2. Assign a specific pay code for recording salary sacrifice savings
  3. Set the percentage of the NI saving that will be passed to employees as an employer top-up (with 100% as the default)

- **How it works**: Once configured, when the system calculates pension figures in forecasts, it automatically includes the employer's NI saving. For example, if an employee sacrifices salary for a pension, the employer saves money on NI contributions (because the sacrificed amount reduces the payroll on which NI is calculated). This saving is then added to the employer's pension contribution and shown in the forecast total.

- **Practical example**: The guide includes a worked example showing how a £17.25 employer NI saving is calculated and combined with the standard employer pension contribution to give a total employer pension contribution figure.

This feature was introduced in an earlier version but updated in v26 to work with budget forecasting reports.

# Summary: Salary Sacrifice NI Saving as Pension Top Up in Budget Forecast

This guide explains how to configure and use the PeopleXD HR system to include National Insurance (NI) savings from salary sacrifice arrangements as pension top-ups in budget forecasts.

**What you'll learn:**

The guide covers the setup process needed to enable the system to automatically calculate and include employer NI savings as additional pension contributions when forecasting pension costs.

**Key configuration steps:**

1. **Pay Code setup** — Identify which pay codes are salary sacrifice arrangements and link them to the appropriate pension scheme
2. **Pension Scheme setup** — Assign a specific pay code where the NI savings will be recorded and set the percentage of NI savings to be passed on as an employer top-up contribution

**How it works:**

Once configured, when the system calculates pension forecasts, it automatically includes the NI saving generated from salary sacrifice arrangements as an additional employer contribution. For example, if an employee sacrifices £125 in salary for pension, the employer saves NI on that amount (e.g., £17.25 at 13.8% NI rate), and this saving is added to the employer's pension contribution figure in the budget forecast.

This feature was introduced to allow Core Budget to report on NI savings that were already being calculated in the payroll system, providing more accurate pension cost forecasting.

This guide teaches users how to manage P11D and P11D(B) forms within the PeopleXD HR system. P11D forms are UK tax documents used to report employee benefits and expenses to HM Revenue & Customs.

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

**Understand the Basics:**
- What P11D and P11D(B) forms are and why they're needed
- Which expenses qualify for tax exemptions
- The filing deadlines for these forms

**Create and Load P11D Data:**
- Import P11D data into PeopleXD using CSV files, including understanding the correct file structure and format
- Navigate the P11D section lettering system used in the forms
- Apply data loading rules correctly

**Configure the System:**
- Set up payroll and expense data to feed into P11D forms
- Map pay codes to the appropriate P11D sections (in both the system's Back Office and Modern UI versions)
- Map expense codes to P11D sections
- Extract benefits data automatically from PeopleXD
- Maintain and update P11D details with proper data rules

**Generate and Submit Forms:**
- Create paper-based versions of P11D and P11D(B) forms for manual submission
- Generate XML files of P11D/P11D(B) forms for electronic submission
- Handle P11D(B) adjustments and Class 1A National Insurance contributions
- Transfer completed XML files to HM Revenue & Customs

The guide provides step-by-step instructions, configuration requirements, and examples throughout.

# Summary: RTI Stability Improvements Guide

This guide explains the updates to Real Time Information (RTI) functionality in CorePay v26. Users will learn about four key improvements that have been made to enhance system stability and prevent data submission errors:

1. **Enhanced Excel Reports** — The Excel file exported from the RTI screen for FPS (Full Payment Submission) files now includes additional data fields: RTI Employee Number and National Insurance Number (NINO).

2. **Improved Exception Reporting** — The RTI exception report has been expanded to catch and flag critical errors before file transfer, including:
   - Missing employee dates of birth
   - Invalid characters in employee initials
   - Address lines exceeding 35 characters
   
   When these issues are flagged, users must correct the employee data and regenerate the FPS file before attempting transfer.

3. **Transfer Safeguards** — The RTI Transfer function now includes a protective mechanism that prevents users from submitting FPS files that contain critical errors identified by the exception report. Users receive warning messages for affected pay groups, and the system requires RTI validation to be completed before any additional payroll processing can occur.

4. **EPS File Generation for Prior Years** — Users can now generate an Employer Payment Summary (EPS) file for previous tax years, which automatically returns the full year-end position as required by HMRC.

**Important note:** These improvements require no new system configuration to implement.

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage the Teachers' Pension Scheme (TPS) within the PeopleXD HR payroll system.

# Summary of "2026/27 Portal" User Guide

This guide covers the UK payroll year end process for the 2026/27 tax year using the PeopleXD HR system portal. It explains the key changes and updates users will need to implement when processing payroll for this period.

## Main Topics Covered:

**Tax Year Rates and Configuration**
- Details on which 2026/27 tax rates come pre-loaded in the system and which rates require manual configuration by customers

**P60 Documentation**
- Information about changes to the P60 form template for this tax year

**Real Time Information (RTI) Submissions**
- Updates to the FPS (Full Payment Submission) and EPS (Employer Payment Summary) schemas that affect how payroll data is reported to HMRC

**Student Loan Changes**
- Introduction of a new Student Loan Plan 5 with a new enumeration code (05)
- Updated student loan thresholds for all plans in 2026/27
- System configuration steps needed to set up Plan 5 pay codes
- Instructions for processing SL1 files (starting deductions) and SL2 files (ending deductions)
- Guidance on student loan reporting
- De Minimis State Aid considerations

**Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) Reform**
- Three major changes to SSP rules effective from 6 April 2026:
  - Abolition of the 3-day waiting period before SSP payments begin
  - Removal of the Lower Earnings Limit, expanding eligibility
  - New SSP flat rate and updated calculation method

The guide includes worked examples and visual comparisons showing before/after scenarios to help users understand these changes.

# Summary: Absence Cut Off User Guide

This guide teaches payroll administrators how to use the **Absence Cut Off feature** in PeopleXD Payroll, which gives them control over whether absence data from the Workforce Management (WFM) system is included when running payroll validation.

**What you'll learn:**

- **What the feature does**: The Absence Cut Off feature allows payroll administrators to run Payroll Validation either with or without pulling through absences that have been recorded in WFM, giving them more control over payroll figures and reports.

- **How to enable it**: Step-by-step instructions for turning on the feature by navigating to Administrator Dashboard > Site Manager > Admin Settings, searching for the setting `cp_manual_absence_run`, and updating its value to 'Y'. (Note: This feature requires Access Engineering to enable a feature flag in your system first.)

- **How to use it on the Payroll Dashboard**: Understanding the visual indicators in the 'Mode' column that show whether WFM absences are currently set to be included (Green) or excluded (Red), and how to use the 3-dot menu to toggle between "Disable WFM Absence" and "Enable WFM Absence" for specific pay groups.

- **How it works in single processing**: When running individual validation runs, users see a new screen with a toggle that matches the pay group's current WFM absence setting, allowing them to choose whether to include or exclude absences for that specific validation.

# Configure Analysis Codes — Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage Analysis Codes in the PeopleXD HR payroll system.

## What you'll learn:

**Understanding Analysis Codes:**
- Analysis Codes are used to group related Pay Codes that share similar characteristics (for example, grouping all absence-related pay codes under "Absence Management" or all basic pay elements under "Basic Pay")
- Every Pay Code must be assigned to an Analysis Code
- Analysis Codes are organised by Analysis Types, which are the main categories used for payroll reporting and financial system integration

**The eight Analysis Types are:**
- GP (Gross Pay)
- NT (Non-Taxable)
- DN (Deduction)
- TR (Tax Relief)
- NP (Nett Pay)
- EN (Employer Pension)
- ER (Employer NI/PRSI)
- AL (Apprentice Levy)

## What you'll be able to do:

1. **Access the Analysis Code screen** — Navigate to the right location in the system and view all existing codes and their details
2. **Filter Analysis Codes** — Use filtering options to search by code, description, analysis type, or pay type
3. **Add new Analysis Codes** — Create custom codes (up to 4 digits) with descriptions to suit your organisation's needs
4. **Delete Analysis Codes** — Remove codes that are no longer needed

The guide also explains that PeopleXD comes with pre-configured Analysis Codes that can be customised, and that these codes are essential for payroll reporting, data extraction, and posting information to your financial management system.

- Configure pay codes, pay groups, and pension schemes for auto enrolment purposes
- Set State Pension Ages
- Configure earnings parameters and pension contribution rules
- Set up default pension scheme rules
- Configure postponement options (delaying auto enrolment for employees)
- Set exclusion rules (preventing certain employees from being auto-enrolled)
- Configure company-level auto enrolment parameters

The guide provides step-by-step instructions for each configuration task, helping payroll administrators ensure their organisation complies with UK auto enrolment regulations through the system.

t: Configure Cost Centres
